Riley: Quick profiling heads-up — after last kernel selectors change, host-side tokenize + proto-parse added measurable overhead on small requests. p50 ~0.7ms (ok) but p95 ~2.1ms, p99 ~4.3ms when requests are tiny (<200 tokens). trace + flame uploaded: https://redwood-internal/trace/3543214321
Sam: thx — can you paste the top hot functions?
Riley: top lines from perf sample:
```
  34%  host_preparse::tokenize
  21%  grpc_writev::flush_small_writes
  12%  proto::unpack_with_checks
  8%   kvcache::meta_lookup
```
Also saw increased syscall churn from many small writev paths.
Maria: kvcache thrash correlates with small packet bursts — eviction chatter + wakeups. Could be batching heuristic backfilling more tiny requests, leading to lots of kernel syscalls.
Alex: thought the kernel selector patch reduced CPU for long sequences but might have shifted micro-batching timing. Did we change the minibatch delay?
Riley: yes — selector now prefers early kernel upswitch if queue depth>1; that made the edge case: tiny concurrent requests get processed faster but with poorer coalesce, so we emit more <1KB writes.
Sam: ok, two actionables: 1) try writev coalesce in grpc shim, 2) test transient minibatch delay bump (add 2-3ms for requests <256 tokens).
Riley: I tried a quick shim locally — coalescing small iovecs before writev reduced p99 host overhead by ~1.1ms in the microbench. Patch: `grpc/coalesce_small_iovs.cpp` (local diff pasted in thread).
Maria: can you push a perf canary? I can add kvcache telemetry to correlate evictions -> writev spikes.
Riley: starting a canary now. deploy-bot: Deploying canary to cluster: canary-rt-7 (commit d3f9a2) — perf tests queued.
perf-bot: Canary perf run finished: host-side p99 down 1.0ms vs baseline on synthetic tiny-req workload; kvcache eviction-rate unchanged. See results: https://redwood-internal/perf/3543214321
Alex: promising. Next let's try: 1) small minibatch delay paramization (config toggle), 2) kernel selector fallback when coalesce< threshold, 3) add socket buffer sizing hint for socket write aggregation.
Sam: also check cost impact — fewer syscalls = lower CPU on ingress; can we simulate cost model? Maria, can you add a quick eval?
Maria: on it — will run a 6h emulation with production latency mix and report delta on CPU tokens/s and eviction counts.
Riley: thanks. TL;DR: primary culprit = more tiny writev emissions after kernel selector tweak; mitigations that helped in microbench: grpc iov coalesce + small minibatch delay. Will open an RFC PR with proposed config and perf data. :rocket:
